tex_content.html:
Theorem
[Solution of gradient flow] ↗ thm:properties-resolvent-yosida ↗ def:nonlinear-contraction-semigroup 1. ch9:9.6-thm-3\group Nonlinear Semigroups

For each $u \in D(\partial I)$ there exists a unique function \[ \mathbf{u} \in C([0, \infty ); H), \text{ with } \mathbf{u}' \in L^\infty (0, \infty ; H), \tag {16} \] such that

  1. $\mathbf{u}(0) = u$,

  2. $\mathbf{u}(t) \in D(\partial I)$ for each $t > 0$,

and

  1. $\mathbf{u}'(t) \in -\partial I[\mathbf{u}(t)]$ for a.e. $t \geq 0$.

Proof

\sketch Solve the regularized ODE $\mathbf u_\lambda '+A_\lambda (\mathbf u_\lambda )=0$. Monotonicity gives contraction, a uniform derivative bound, and a Cauchy estimate as $\lambda \downarrow 0$, producing a continuous limit with bounded derivative. Passing the subdifferential inequality to the limit shows $-\mathbf u'(t)\in \partial I[\mathbf u(t)]$ and closedness gives domain membership at every time. Monotonicity applied to two solutions yields uniqueness.

□
